visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: In a bank, which team owns the long-term client relationship?
questions.explain: Coverage bankers know their companies for years; product teams such as mergers and acquisitions bring the specialist execution when a deal happens.
questions.explain_at: Coverage teams are organised by industry

questions.q: Kraft paid a special dividend of $16.50 a share. How much cash did 100 shares receive?
questions.explain: 100 × $16.50 = $1,650. The $10bn total, funded by 3G and Berkshire, was spread across all of Kraft's shares.
questions.explain_at: a special cash dividend of sixteen dollars and fifty cents

questions.q: Is a private equity firm like Carlyle an investment bank?

options.text: Yes, investment banks invest in companies
Yes, it's a type of bulge-bracket bank
No, it's an elite boutique adviser
No, it buys companies with its own funds

questions.explain: Private equity firms buy companies with their own funds. Banks advise them and lend to them, which is why banks have a financial sponsors group.
questions.explain_at: Third misunderstanding. Investment banks mostly don't invest

questions.q: A company wants to list its shares for the first time. Which product team runs that?
questions.explain: An IPO raises equity, so ECM runs it. Mergers and acquisitions advises when control of a company changes hands.
questions.explain_at: E-C-M, equity capital markets, helps companies raise money

questions.q: Kraft Heinz promised $1.5bn of annual cost savings. At ten times, what are they worth?

options.text: $15bn, less the cost of getting them

questions.explain: 1.5 × 10 = $15bn, before the cost of actually achieving the savings. Kraft Heinz cut hard, but the brands stopped growing.
questions.explain_at: They promised one and a half billion dollars a year of cost savings
